sam_devx: Quick report: our Python AsyncClient is dropping request-id/correlation when retries or background tasks run. Minimal repro below.

sam_devx: ```py
from contextvars import ContextVar
from redwood import AsyncClient
req = ContextVar('request_id')
async def main():
    req.set('r-123')
    c = AsyncClient(retry_policy={'max_attempts':2}, instrumentor_enabled=True)
    await c.generate_async('hi')  # logs in attempt 2 missing request_id
```

yara_sdk: Thanks. Likely root cause: tasks spawned for backoff/exporter/batcher aren't copying contextvars (we recently used anyio/TaskGroup in some paths). Two-pronged fix: 1) central _spawn_task helper that uses context.copy_context().run(create_task,..), 2) small, typed observability hook API as an escape hatch.

vince_infra: For the hook shape we prefer a Protocol for typing ergonomics:
```
class ObsCallback(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, event: str, attrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Optional[Awaitable[None]]: ...
```
Client.register_observer('emit_log', cb) should accept sync or async callables; SDK will await if cb returns awaitable.

nora_obs: Also add convenience helpers: client.bind_contextvar('request_id', req) and client.instrument_opentelemetry(map_baggage=fn) so common integrations are trivial. Include examples and a perf note: awaiting callbacks on hot paths can add latency.

yara_sdk: Action items: (A) implement minimal _spawn_task and migrate retry/backoff and batcher, (B) add ObsCallback Protocol + register_observer as follow-up, (C) add a sample-app integration test: set ContextVar, force transient error to trigger retry, assert logs and OTEL span/baggage include request_id, (D) short doc note for onboarding. I'll open a draft PR.
